subject.title: [TUI] Scroll-jump / auto-scroll behavior is still disruptive in 2026.3.8

question: What should the TUI default follow policy be when new content arrives while the user is reading older transcript content?
rationale: Current source supports the report, but choosing between default reader-position preservation, bottom-follow behavior, and a new TUI preference changes user-facing terminal UX and possibly config/settings surface.

options.title: Define anchor policy, then fix
options.body: Keep this issue as the broad TUI tracker, specify the desired default and jump-to-latest behavior, then implement the smallest renderer/TUI change with PTY and live terminal proof.

options.title: Narrow to renderer bug only
options.body: Treat the remaining work as pi-tui scrollback/full-redraw repair and leave any explicit TUI auto-scroll preference for a later product issue.

options.title: Add a TUI preference
options.body: Add a user-facing TUI follow/auto-scroll mode, accepting the added settings/config surface and upgrade-proof burden.

recommendation.title: Define anchor policy, then fix
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the broad TUI tracker, specify the desired default and jump-to-latest behavior, then implement the smallest renderer/TUI change with PTY and live terminal proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is primarily TUI UX/product policy, and steipete appears in current history for the TUI kit, TUI refresh performance, and adjacent TUI fixes.
